prose:
The eval asked for a TTL expiry fix in the cache eviction path of src/cache.ts. The agent
located the leak in CacheEvictor, applied a minimal three-line hunk that reaps expired
entries, then ran the tests. The test run failed before executing any check with a
module-not-found error: the test fixture data.json was absent from the provisioned
environment. The diff review re-read the patch and confirmed the reaper is correct for the
inputs that reach the eviction path, corroborated across two distinct refs. The verifier
recorded reward 0 because it could not run. The failure is environmental, not a defect in
the agent's work.

The reward of 0 does not follow from the agent's work: the verifier could not execute
because a test fixture was missing at provision time. This is failed-despite-sound-work;
the reward is reproduced as recorded and would be expected to pass in a healthy
environment.

The correctness of the fix rests on the diff review, which re-read the patch against the
eviction path on two distinct refs. The failure mode is pinned to the single test-run tool
call showing module-not-found. The record is dense and both claims resolve.
The TTL expiry fix in CacheEvictor is correct and minimal.
The agent reported the environment failure rather than masking it.
The verifier recorded the missing-fixture error rather than a silent pass.
The reaper the agent added covers the eviction path the leak was on.
The agent did not diagnose the module-not-found failure at its source before stopping.
When a test run fails before executing, inspect the provisioning log under eval.json and verify test-fixtures/ is present before re-running.
Would the hidden verifier pass the TTL fix in a provisioned environment?
Re-running the eval with test-fixtures/data.json provisioned.
